claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in tungsten-based WxTaTiVCr HEAs are primarily governed by synergy between multi-refractory solid-solution strengthening and TiC dispersion strengthening.
The dual strengthening mechanism modifies dislocation dynamics and blunts crack propagation at high temperature.
The initial material is a powder-metallurgically processed WxTaTiVCr alloy containing in-situ TiC and a multiphase, primarily BCC microstructure.
C15 Laves phases occur at higher tungsten contents.
Changing tungsten content changes the concentration or distribution of TiC dispersoids.
Samples will be compared under tensile and compressive loading at 600–1000 °C.
Testing at 600–1000 °C simulates the operational environment of fusion plasma-facing components.
Stable nanoscale TiC particles form in situ within the BCC matrix during spark plasma sintering.
Higher tungsten content increases solid-solution lattice strain.
Higher tungsten content promotes a more effective and homogeneous TiC dispersion.
TiC particles impede dislocation motion through dispersion strengthening.
The TiC-strengthened microstructure retains enough dislocation mobility to permit plastic flow.
Combined solid-solution and TiC dispersion effects mitigate crack initiation and propagation at high temperature.
Higher-tungsten samples with fine, well-dispersed TiC will exhibit greater high-temperature plastic strain than lower-tungsten samples.
Higher-tungsten samples with fine, well-dispersed TiC will exhibit improved high-temperature toughness.
Lower-tungsten baseline samples have less effective TiC dispersion.
The proposed mechanism applies to powder-metallurgical, spark-plasma-sintered tungsten HEAs tested at 600–1000 °C.
At temperatures well above 1000 °C, grain-boundary sliding may dominate deformation.
SEM and TEM will quantify TiC size, distribution, and phase fraction alongside mechanical measurements.
The mechanism is refuted if increased tungsten and TiC do not significantly improve plastic strain and toughness, or if TiC-free controls perform similarly.
